q: What is once in a minute, twice in a moment, and never in a thousand years?
What is it that when you take away the whole, you still have some left over?
What two things can you never eat for breakfast?
What word can be written forward, backward or upside down, and can still be read from left to right?
They have not flesh, nor feathers, nor scales, nor bone. Yet they have fingers and thumbs of their own. What are they?
I am large as a castle, yet lighter than air. 100 men and their horses cannot move me. What am I?
This is as light as a feather, Yet no man can hold it for long. What is it?
What is put on a table, cut, but never eaten?
Whoever makes it, tells it not. Whoever takes it, knows it not. And whoever knows it wants it not.
What can go up a chimney down, but cannot go down a chimney up?
What never gets any wetter, no matter how much it rains?
No sooner spoken than broken. What is it?
When they are caught, they are thrown away. When they escape, you itch all day. What are they?
You hear it speak, for it has a hard tongue. But it cannot breathe, for it has not a lung. What is it?
What is it that is deaf, dumb and blind and always tells the truth?
What gets whiter the dirtier that it gets?
Which word in the English language becomes shorter when it is lengthened?
What is red and blue, and purple and green? No one can reach it, not even the queen?
At night they come without being fetched, And by day they are lost without being stolen.
What is round on the ends and high in the middle?
Different lights do make me strange, thus into different sizes I will change. What am I?
a: I am the pupil of an eye

q: You have three stoves: a gas stove, a wood stove, and a coal stove, but only one match. Which should you light first?
What always goes to bed with shoes on?
Who is it that rows quickly with four oars but never comes out from under his own roof?
You use it between your head and your toes, the more it works the thinner it grows. What is it?
What object has keys that open no locks, space but no room, and you can enter but not go in?
Big as a biscuit, deep as a cup, even a river can't fill it up. What is it?
What has one foot on each side and one in the middle?
What common English verb becomes its own past tense by rearranging its letters?
What part of the turkey has the most feathers?
I know a word of letters three. Add two, and fewer there will be.
What's the greatest worldwide use of cowhide?
What word contains all of the twenty six letters?
What goes up when the rain comes down?
Where will you find roads without cars, forests without trees and cities without houses?
What has roots that nobody sees, and is taller than trees. Up, up it goes, and yet it never grows. What is it?
How can you physically stand behind your friend as he physically stands behind you?
The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?
Walk on the living, they don't even mumble. Walk on the dead, they mutter and grumble. What are they?
If a rooster laid a brown egg and a white egg, what kind of chicks would hatch?
What gets wetter the more it dries?
You can't keep this until you have given it.
The sun bakes them, the hand breaks them, the foot treads on them, and the mouth tastes them. What are they?
You can see nothing else When you look in my face, I will look you in the eye And I will never lie.
At the sound of me, men may dream, Or stamp their feet. At the sound of me, women may laugh, Or sometimes weep.
How could a cowboy ride into town on Friday, stay two days, and ride out on Friday?
I have an eye but cannot see. I am stronger and faster then any man alive but have no limbs. What am I?
What goes up and never comes down?
My life can be measured in hours, I serve by being devoured. Thin, I am quick Fat, I am slow Wind is my foe.
Weight in my belly, Trees on my back. Nails in my ribs, Feet I do lack.
You heard me before, Yet you hear me again. Then I die, 'Til you call me again What am I?
What is harder to catch the faster you run?
What is it that you ought to keep after you have given it to someone else?
If life gets tough, what do you have that you can always count on?
A hundred feet in the air, but it's back is on the ground. What is it?
What kind of coat can be put on only when wet?
Lighter than what I am made of. More of me is hidden than seen.
What can go up and come down without moving?
I turn around once. What is out will not get in. I turn around again. What is in will not get out. What am I?
What starts with a T, ends with a T, and has T in it?
What do you serve that you can't eat?
Until I am measured, I am not known. Yet how you miss me, When I have flown. What am I?
What kind of running means walking?
What's as big as you are yet doesn't weigh an ounce?
You must keep this thing, its loss will affect your brothers. For once yours is lost, it will soon be lost by others.
I am always hungry, I must always be fed, The finger I lick Will soon turn red.
Until I am measured, I am not known. Yet how you miss me, When I have flown.
I am only useful When I am full, Yet I am always Full of holes.
If a man carried my burden He would break his back. I am not rich, But leave silver in my track.
I am weightless, but you can see me. Put me in a bucket, and I'll make it lighter. What am I?
Where on Earth do the winds always blow from the South?
What can you catch but not throw?
I am a box that holds keys without locks, yet they can unlock your soul. What am I?
Who spends the day at the window, goes to the table for meals and hides at night?
What has garbage and flies?
its is the beginning of existence and the end of time, its the beginning of everything and the end of space, what am i?
A father's child, a mother's child, yet no one's son. Who am I.
I am a fathers child and a mothers child, yet I am not a son. Who am I?
When I point up it's bright, but when I point down it's dark. What am I?
The strangest creature you'll ever find: Two eyes in front and many many more behind.
I have no legs or arms but I still eat with a fork everyday, What am I?
What fastens two people yet touches only one?
You can carry it everywhere you go, and it does not get heavy. What is it?
I am six letters. When you take one away I am twelve. What am I?
What falls but doesn't break, and what breaks but doesn't fall?
I can be cracked, I can be made. I can be told, I can be played. What am I?
{ I GO UP AND DOWN.... BUT NEVER MOVE. WHO AM I?
No legs have I to dance, No lungs have I to breathe, No life have I to live or die And yet I do all three. What am I?
What goes into the water black and comes out red?
Here on Earth it's always true, that a day follows a day. But there is a place where yesterday always follows today!
What time is it when the clock strikes 13?
a: Time to get the clock fixed

q: How Far Can You Walk into the woods?
What has a head, a tail, is brown, and has no legs?
I'm a god, a planet, and measurer of heat. Who am I?
Who are the two brothers who live on opposite sides of the road yet never see each other?
If a man carried my burden he would break his back. I am not big but leave silver in my tracks. What am I?
What is the color of the vest's sleeves?...
Almost everyone sees me without noticing me, For what is beyond is what he or she seeks. What am I?

What kind of storm is always in a rush?
What sport has four letters, is played all around the world, and begins with a T?
What is so fragile that when you say its name you break it?
What is round as a dishpan, deep as a tub, and still the oceans couldn't fill it up?
I fly, yet I have no wings. I cry, yet I have no eyes. Darkness follows me; lower light I never see.
What has to be broken before it can be used?

what is black when clean and white when dirty?
What has a head and a tail, but no body?
What has an eye but cannot see?
What kind of room has no doors or windows?
What has a tongue but cannot talk?
What has a bed but never sleeps?
What has a mouth but never eats?
What always runs but never walks?
What has a face but no eyes?
What has hands but can't clap?
What starts with T, ends with T and has T in it?
What has a bank but no money?
What has a spine but no bones?

What starts with an E, ends with an E and only has one letter in it?
I am not alive, but I grow; I don't have lungs, but I need air; What am I?
I can go up and down without moving.
What has a neck but no head?

Can you name three consecutive days without using the words Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, or Sunday?

What is the easiest way to throw a ball, and have it stop, and completely reverse direction after traveling a short distance?
There is an ancient invention still used in some parts of the world today that allows people to see through walls. What is it?
I have a big mouth and I am also quite loud! I am NOT a gossip but I do get involved with everyone's dirty business. Can you name me?
Be you ever so quick, with vision keen, by your eyes, we are never seen. Unless perchance it should come to pass, you see our reflection in a looking glass. What are we?
Here on earth it is true, yesterday is always before today; but there is a place where yesterday always follows today. Where?
Hands she has but does not hold, teeth she has but does not bite, feet she has but they are cold, eyes she has but without sight. Who is she?
There was a green house. Inside the green house there was a white house Inside the white house there was a red house. Inside the red house there were lots of babies.
What question can someone ask all day long, always get completely different answers, and yet all the answers could be correct?
In spring I am gay in handsome array; in summer more clothing I wear; when colder it grows I fling off my clothes; and in winter quite naked appear. What am I?
Violet, indigo, blue and green, yellow, orange and red; these are the colors you have seen after the storm has fled.What am I?
Old Mother Twitchett had but one eye, and a long tail which she let fly; and every time she went through a gap, a bit of her tail she left in a trap. What is she?
Never resting, never still. Moving silently from hill to hill. It does not walk, run or trot, All is cool where it is not. What is it?
I am taken from a mine, and shut up in a wooden case, from which I am never released, and yet I am used by almost everybody.
As I went across the bridge, I met a man with a load of wood which was neither straight nor crooked. What kind of wood was it?
I can be long, or I can be short. I can be grown, and I can be bought. I can be painted, or left bare. I can be round, or square. What am I?
I have two arms, but fingers none. I have two feet, but cannot run. I carry well, but I have found I carry best with my feet OFF the ground. What am I?
there is a man he leaves home and runs around three blocks, when he comes back home their are two masked men, who are they?
What force and strength cannot get through I with a gentle touch can do, And many in the street would stand were I not a friend in hand.
My voice is tender, my waist is slender and I'm often invited to play. Yet wherever I go I must take my bow or else I have nothing to say. What am I?
I have a little house in which I live all alone. It has no doors or windows, and if I want to go out I must break through the wall.
I can flutter and take your breath away. I can take a beating, but do not bruise. If I stopped you would be sure to lose. Everyday I am with you. What am I?
My thunder comes before the lightning; My lightning comes before the clouds; My rain dries all the land it touches. What am I?
I come at the end of time and at the start of eternitiy. I come four times in every week, but only once in a thousand years. What am I?
I wag my tail when I am happy and love to play fetch in the yard. I bark to greet my family. What am I?
I purr when you pet me and meow when it is dinner time. I love chasing yarn and napping in the sun. What am I?
I chew green grass in the pasture and give cold milk every day. I make a loud moo sound. What am I?
I wear iron shoes on my hooves and carry a saddle on my back. I neigh as I gallop across the field. What am I?
I have a curly tail and a flat pink snout. I love to roll around in cool mud and say oink. What am I?
My fluffy wool is sheared each spring to make warm sweaters. I graze in a flock and say baa. What am I?
I have two horns, a little beard, and love climbing steep hills on the farm. I make a bleating sound. What am I?
I have long ears and carry heavy packs on dirt trails. My loud braying call sounds like hee-haw. What am I?
I have a bright red comb on my head and colorful feathers. I wake up the farm at dawn with a loud crow. What am I?
I have orange webbed feet and paddle across the farm pond. I love to splash in water and say quack. What am I?
I have a long neck, large wings, and make a loud honking sound. I can be a feisty guard bird on the farm. What am I?
I am a large farm bird with a red wattle under my beak. I spread my tail into a fan and gobble loudly. What am I?
I have long ears, a twitchy nose, and a fluffy cotton tail. I hop quickly and love eating carrots. What am I?
I stuff seeds into my stretchy cheek pouches. At night, I run fast on an exercise wheel in my cage. What am I?
I am a plump pet rodent with no tail at all. I make a happy wheek sound whenever I hear crisp vegetables. What am I?
I have shiny orange scales and breathe through gills. I swim in a glass bowl and eat tiny flakes of food. What am I?
I have brightly colored feathers and a hooked beak. I can learn to mimic human speech and repeat words. What am I?
I carry a hard, protective shell on my back. When I am frightened, I tuck my head and legs safely inside. What am I?
I am a tiny pet with a long, thin tail and big round ears. I love to nibble cheese and make quiet squeaks. What am I?
I have a long, flexible body and love darting through tubes. I am a playful pet related to the weasel family. What am I?
I am a small pet bird with bright yellow feathers. People love to keep me in their homes for my cheerful singing. What am I?
I have a long neck, thick wool, and guard sheep on the farm. If you make me angry, I might spit at you! What am I?
I am a pet lizard with sticky toe pads that let me climb up smooth walls. I lick my eyes to keep them clean. What am I?
I carry a borrowed sea shell on my back as my home. When I grow bigger, I have to find a larger shell to move into. What am I?

I am a flightless bird dressed in a black-and-white tuxedo. I love to slide on icy belly trails and swim in cold water. What am I?

I am a tall wading bird with bright pink feathers. I often rest by balancing on just one skinny leg in the water. What am I?
I move through rainforest trees so slowly that green algae grows on my fur. I spend my life hanging upside down. What am I?
I am a fuzzy Australian marsupial with big round ears. I love to snooze in trees and munch eucalyptus leaves. What am I?
I have thick white fur and webbed paws for swimming in freezing Arctic waters. I am the world's biggest bear. What am I?

I am a male bird famous for fanning out a huge tail of shimmering feathers covered in colorful eyespots. What am I?
I am a black-and-white bear from China. I spend almost all day sitting down and crunching on green bamboo stalks. What am I?
I am a heavy, thick-skinned plant-eater with one or two horns on my snout. I love rolling in cool mud. What am I?

I am the largest of all primates. The wise male leader of my troop is called a silverback. What am I?

I buzz around flowers collecting sweet nectar and pollen. Back in my hive, I make sweet honey. What am I?

I am a tiny insect that lives underground in a huge colony. I can carry items much heavier than myself. What am I?

I am a small, round beetle with bright red wing covers decorated with black spots. What am I?

I am a small fish with a head shaped like a horse and a curly tail that grips onto sea grass. What am I?
I have a hard shell, walk sideways along the ocean floor, and snap two big pincers. What am I?
I am a small orange fish with white stripes. I live safely among the stinging tentacles of sea anemones. What am I?
I am a yellow fruit that monkeys love to eat. You have to peel my skin before taking a bite. What am I?
I am an orange vegetable that grows underground. Rabbits love to crunch on me, and I have a leafy green top. What am I?

I am huge and green on the outside, but pink and juicy on the inside with black seeds. What am I?

I share my name with my color. Peel off my thick rind to find sweet, juicy slices full of vitamin C. What am I?
I look like a bunch of tiny green trees on your plate. Kids love to dip my florets into ranch dressing. What am I?
I am round and red, and people often call me a vegetable. I am crushed to make ketchup and pizza sauce. What am I?
I wear a green husk and have yellow kernels all in a row. Heat me up in a pan, and I will pop! What am I?
I am an oval yellow fruit that is very sour. Squeeze my juice into water with sugar to make a cool drink. What am I?

I am a long, cool green vegetable with watery flesh. If you soak me in vinegar and dill, I turn into a pickle. What am I?
I have prickly skin and wear a crown of spiky green leaves. Inside, my yellow fruit is sweet and tangy. What am I?
I am a small, round green ball that grows in a pod with my twins. You often find me mixed with diced carrots. What am I?
I am a sweet summer fruit covered in soft, fuzzy skin. Inside, I have juicy orange flesh and a large pit. What am I?

I am a long, crunchy green stalk with leaves on top. People love to fill me with peanut butter. What am I?

I wear a yellow jacket that you peel off to eat my sweet white fruit. What am I?

Mice love to nibble on me, and I melt into gooey goodness on top of your pizza. What am I?

I am a long, crunchy orange vegetable that grows in the ground and rabbits love to crunch. What am I?
I am baked flat and round in an oven, covered with tomato sauce and cheese, then cut into triangles. What am I?
I am a bright, sweet breakfast drink squeezed fresh from round citrus fruits. What am I?
I am a thick brown spread made from crushed nuts, and I love pairing up with jelly in sandwiches. What am I?

I grow underground with brown skin, and you can bake me, mash me, or slice me into french fries. What am I?
Busy bees make me from flower nectar, and I am sticky, golden, and sweet in your tea. What am I?
I have a hard green rind outside, juicy red fruit inside, and tiny black seeds you spit out. What am I?
I am a bright yellow fruit that makes your lips pucker, but add sugar to my juice and you get a cool summer drink. What am I?

I am baked round and sweet with chocolate chips, and I taste great when you dunk me in cold milk. What am I?
I am a sweet red berry shaped like a heart, and my tiny seeds are worn on the outside of my skin. What am I?
I come in a yellow stick wrapped in paper, and I melt smoothly over hot toast and ears of corn. What am I?
I sit in a cardboard box, waiting to rattle into your morning bowl before the milk pours over me. What am I?
I am a warm, sweet brown drink that warms you up on snowy days, especially with marshmallows on top. What am I?
I am a shiny red fruit often called a vegetable, and I get crushed to make ketchup and pizza sauce. What am I?
I grow in sweet purple or green bunches on a vine, and if you dry me out I become a raisin. What am I?
I have many papery layers, and when you chop me up in the kitchen, I might make your eyes cry. What am I?
I beat like a drum inside your chest and pump blood throughout your body. What am I?
I sit safely inside your skull, helping you think, learn, and remember things. What am I?
We take in fresh oxygen when you breathe in and push out air when you breathe out. What are we?
I churn up the food you swallow and sometimes make a loud growl when you are hungry. What am I?
I am the sturdy frame made of all your bones that keeps you from being floppy. What am I?
We pull on your bones to help you run, jump, smile, and carry your heavy backpack. What are we?
I am the largest organ of your body, covering you from head to toe to keep germs out. What am I?
I am the bright red liquid flowing through your veins to deliver oxygen to your body. What am I?
We let you see bright colors and shapes, and we blink to stay moist and clean. What are we?
We catch sounds so you can listen to music, and we also help you keep your balance. What are we?
I sit right in the middle of your face to help you smell flowers and sneeze out dust. What am I?
I help you talk, swallow, and taste whether a snack is sweet, salty, or sour. What am I?
We line your mouth in neat white rows to help you bite and chew up crunchy apples. What are we?
We have five fingers each, and you use us to write, wave hello, and catch a ball. What are we?
We have five toes each and fit into your sneakers to help you run and kick. What are we?
I am the important joint in the middle of your leg that bends when you squat or pedal. What am I?
I am the bendable joint halfway down your arm that lets you touch your own shoulder. What am I?
I sprout on top of your head, and you can brush, wash, or snip me without feeling a thing. What am I?
We are hard shields growing at the ends of your fingers that you can clip and paint. What are we?
We form a curved cage around your chest to keep your heart and lungs safe from harm. What are we?
I am the column of small bones down your back that holds you upright and protects your spinal cord. What am I?
I am the little dent or bump on your tummy that marks where you were connected before you were born. What am I?
We sit just above your eyes to catch forehead sweat and help you show surprise. What are we?
We are short little hairs on the edges of your eyelids that keep dust from blowing into your eyes. What are we?
We are clear, salty drops that wash over your eyes and spill onto your cheeks when you cry. What are we?
You make me using your vocal cords whenever you whisper a secret, laugh out loud, or sing. What am I?
I am a giant ball of hot gas that lights up your day. Earth travels around me. What am I?
I glow in the night sky and change my shape from a crescent to a full circle. What am I?

Hold my two handles and swing me over your head, then hop as I sweep beneath your feet. What am I?
I lie flat between paper pages so you never lose your place in an adventure story. What am I?
I come in a box with interlocking cardboard pieces that fit together into a big picture. What am I?
I have a long ribbon tail and paper diamond wings, dancing high whenever the wind blows. What am I?
I am a colorful plastic ring you spin around your waist without letting me hit the ground. What am I?
My pages are filled with black outlines waiting for you to shade them in with bright colors. What am I?
I am a stick of colored wax wrapped in paper. I get shorter the more pictures you draw. What am I?
I hang from two chains on the playground. Pump your legs back and forth to fly high. What am I?
Climb up my ladder to the very top, sit down, and swoosh smoothly to the bottom. What am I?
I am a small plastic block with round studs on top that snaps together to build towers. What am I?
I tell action stories using speech bubbles, sound effects, and illustrated panels. What am I?
I am a shiny glass ball with swirls inside. Flick me with your thumb to knock targets away. What am I?
I am a wooden board on four small wheels with rough grip tape on top. Kick and coast away! What am I?
Turn my crank to hear a tune, then laugh when a funny puppet pops out through my lid. What am I?
Turn my heavy pages and watch cardboard castles and dragons spring up into 3D shapes. What am I?
I am made of soap and water, floating softly through the air until a single tap pops me. What am I?
I am a wooden pit filled with golden grains where kids dig with shovels and build castles. What am I?
I am a coiled spring made of metal or plastic that can walk down stairs all by myself. What am I?
Slip your fingers inside my cloth body and move my mouth so I can talk during a story. What am I?
I am a plank balanced in the center. When your friend goes up into the air, you go down. What am I?
Fill my stretchy rubber skin from a hose, tie a knot, and throw me for a soaking splash. What am I?
I am a thick reference book arranged from A to Z to explain what words mean and how to spell them. What am I?
I have tiny rooms, miniature chairs, and a small front door, but no real people live in me. What am I?
I come in a bright yellow tub, squish easily in your hands, and can be molded into any shape. What am I?
I have a bed but I never sleep. I have a running mouth that never speaks. What am I?
I am a river that suddenly takes a great leap over high rocks. I crash with a roar below. What am I?
I am like a tiny river that bubbles over smooth stones in the forest. You can easily step over me. What am I?
I am taller than any tree or building and touch the clouds. My peak is often covered in snow. What am I?
I look like a regular mountain until I rumble and blow my top. Hot red lava spills down my sides. What am I?
I am a dark hollow space hidden deep inside a rocky mountain. Bats often hang from my ceiling. What am I?
I am a deep desert gorge with steep cliff walls carved by a river over millions of years. What am I?
I am a giant river of solid blue ice that creeps very slowly down a cold mountain. What am I?
I cover most of our blue planet with salty water. Whales and dolphins call me home. What am I?
The ocean wind pushes me toward the shore. I curl, crash into white foam, and wash over your feet. What am I?
I am where the sea meets the land, covered in soft golden sand and shells. What am I?
I was once the hard home of a little sea creature. Now I wash ashore, and you can hear the ocean inside me. What am I?
I am a piece of green land with salty sea water all around me. You need a boat or a plane to visit me. What am I?
I am a giant chunk of floating ice in the freezing ocean. Most of my massive body is hidden underwater. What am I?
I am an underwater city made of colorful living creatures where clownfish and sea turtles play. What am I?
The moon pulls my water up the beach and then pushes it back out twice every day. What am I?
I stand tall on rocky shores and shine a bright turning light to guide ships safely through the dark. What am I?
Kids build me on the shore using damp sand and plastic buckets before the waves wash me away. What am I?
I wake up the earth after a cold sleep. Flowers bloom and baby birds hatch in my sunshine. What season am I?
I bring long sunny days, pool trips, and no school. Ice cream melts quickly during my hottest weeks. What season am I?
Green leaves turn red and gold before dropping from the trees. Farmers harvest pumpkins as the air cools. What season am I?
I bring freezing winds, bare trees, and frosty mornings. Children bundle up in coats to build snowmen. What season am I?
I fall softly from winter clouds with six icy points. No two of me are ever exactly alike. What am I?
